- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; cap forecast at +10–15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment is mixed or trending sideways, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast should be closer to recent 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases (last 7–10 days); apply a 2–5% upward bias if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns positive after a dip, model lags in recognizing momentum — forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for the next 3–5 days.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 14-day low if sentiment is positive — model tends to underestimate recovery.
